blocks.orig:
Zanzibar: Where Beach Honeymoon
Meets Safari Adventure!
blocks.html:
Zanzibar: a beach honeymoon
joined by safari adventure!

blocks.orig: Zanzibar might be one of the best beach honeymoon destinations of the world… beautiful white sandy beaches and coral reefs, comfortable accommodations, and transparent blue sea, like in the movies.
blocks.html: Few places in the world suit a beach honeymoon as well as Zanzibar… gorgeous white sand and coral reefs, comfortable places to stay and clear blue water, just like in a film.

blocks.orig: And did you know? Zanzibar is located only 15 miles off the coast of Tanzania. Which means that you can quickly and easily fly to the Tanzanian mainland and go on an amazing wildlife safari, meet the Tanzanian population, discover their culture and see a lot of animals. This is your chance to meet the Big 5!
blocks.html: Here is something you may not know: Zanzibar lies just 15 miles off the Tanzanian coast. So a short, simple flight takes you to the mainland of Tanzania for a wonderful wildlife safari, where you can meet Tanzanians, learn about their culture and see plenty of animals. It is your opportunity to see the Big 5!

blocks.orig: Safari and beach holiday: is this your dream vacation?
blocks.html: A safari plus a beach holiday: is that the trip you dream of?

blocks.orig: Imagine a dream holiday to the tropical island Zanzibar.  This bounty island is a paradise, offering the world’s most beautiful beaches and coral reefs. Miles and miles of white sandy beaches sprinkled with palm trees, surrounded by the clear azure waters of the Indian Ocean. Apart from laid-back beach life, Zanzibar also has a colorful culture and history. Stone Town is well worth a visit. This fascinating old city offers so many nice markets, restaurants and historical sightseeing’s.
blocks.html: Picture a dream holiday on the tropical island of Zanzibar.  This bounty island is a true paradise, with some of the loveliest beaches and coral reefs anywhere. Endless stretches of white sand dotted with palm trees, lapped by the clear azure water of the Indian Ocean. Besides relaxed beach life, the island has a colourful history and culture too. A visit to Stone Town is well worthwhile. The captivating old town is full of pleasant markets, restaurants and historic sights.

blocks.orig: Zanzibar Island is part of the Zanzibar archipelago, together with Pemba and Mafia and many smaller islands. These islands are also called the Spice Islands because of their rich history in the spice trade and many spice plantations. Great beach destinations to wash off the dust after your safari.
blocks.html: Together with Pemba, Mafia and lots of smaller islands, Zanzibar Island forms the Zanzibar archipelago. People also call them the Spice Islands, after their long history in the spice trade and their numerous spice plantations. They make wonderful beach destinations for washing off the safari dust.

blocks.orig: Zanzibar offers the world’s most beautiful beaches. Soft white sandy beaches surrounded by colourful coral reefs and the crystal clear waters of the Indian Ocean. Zanzibar island has about 25 beaches, sprinkled with fishing villages. Should you stay north or rather choose the south or east coast of Zanzibar?
blocks.html: Some of the loveliest beaches in the world are found on Zanzibar. Think soft white sand, bordered by colourful coral reefs and the crystal-clear Indian Ocean. The island counts around 25 beaches, with fishing villages scattered along them. Will you stay in the north, or would the south or east coast of Zanzibar suit you better?

blocks.orig:
North:
Zanzibar’s best beaches are on the north and east coast of the island, all with crystal white sand and colourful coral reefs. Nungwi and Kendwa are one of the most popular beaches since they do not have to deal with high and low tides. It has a chilled atmosphere with numbers of restaurants, bars and accommodation options. So if you seek real peace and privacy you should visit another part of the island (like the east or south). The north is home to villages like Uroa, Pongwe, Kiwengwa, Nungwi and Kendwa.
blocks.html:
North:
The finest beaches on Zanzibar lie along the north and east coasts, each with brilliant white sand and colourful coral reefs. Nungwi and Kendwa are among the most popular beaches, as the tides there are not an issue. The mood is relaxed, and there are plenty of restaurants, bars and places to stay. If real peace and privacy is what you want, you are better off in another area of the island (such as the east or south). Villages in the north include Uroa, Pongwe, Kiwengwa, Nungwi and Kendwa.

blocks.orig:
East:
At the east coast of the island you will find the most idyllic beaches. Along the eastern coastline runs a beautiful coral reef, a top world spot for snorkelling and diving. You can immerse yourself in the abundance of marine life, such as sea horses, turtles and many tropical fish. The beaches at this east coast are very tidal. During low tide you can take a walk on the beach and enjoy the ocean views. If you love wind- or kite surfing this is the right place for you. Matemwe beach is the longest and one of the most beautiful ones at this site of the island. Like in the north, there is a wealth of accommodation options.
blocks.html:
East:
The east coast is where the most idyllic beaches are. A lovely coral reef stretches along this coastline, one of the world's top places for snorkelling and diving. Here you can dive into rich marine life, including sea horses, turtles and many tropical fish. Tides on the east coast are strong. At low tide you can stroll along the beach and take in the views of the ocean. For fans of windsurfing or kitesurfing, this is the place to be. On this side of the island, Matemwe beach is the longest and one of the loveliest. As in the north, you can choose from a wide range of accommodation.

blocks.orig:
South-East:
This part of the island is known for its long stretch of soft sandy beaches. It is the best spot on the island for sailing or kite- and windsurfing, thanks to steady winds. Hop on a traditional wooden sailboat (dhow) and sail the ocean, or go swimming with dolphins at Kizimkazi (south). Here you will find little villages like Jambiani, Paje and Bwejuu. These small fishing village have a nice timeless atmosphere with friendly people. One of our favourite villages is Jambiani. Check out why we think Jambiani is the place to be in Zanzibar.
blocks.html:
South-East:
This area is famous for its long stretches of soft sand. Thanks to the constant winds, it is the best part of the island for sailing, kitesurfing and windsurfing. Board a traditional wooden sailing boat (dhow) to head out to sea, or swim with dolphins at Kizimkazi (south). This is where you find small villages such as Jambiani, Paje and Bwejuu. These little fishing villages have a pleasant, timeless feel and friendly residents. Jambiani is one of the villages we like best. Find out why we believe Jambiani is the place to be on Zanzibar.

blocks.orig:
South-West:
The south west coast is a bit more remote with fewer lodges and deserted beaches. The beaches in west and south of Zanzibar are less popular, although there are some beautiful beaches with gentle tides. If you visit the south, do not forget to go to Menia Bay Conservation Area. This is a spectacular underwater world for divers. The western coast is home to the fascinating old Stone Town, the cultural and historical centre of Zanzibar.
blocks.html:
South-West:
On the south-west coast things are a little more remote, with fewer lodges and empty beaches. The west and south of Zanzibar draw fewer visitors, although you will find some lovely beaches with mild tides. If you head south, make sure you visit the Menia Bay Conservation Area, a spectacular underwater world for divers. The west coast is where you find the captivating old Stone Town, the historical and cultural heart of Zanzibar.

blocks.orig: The tropical island of Zanzibar is known for its beautiful white sandy beaches and coral reefs. But Zanzibar does not only offer laid-back beach life and watersport activities but also a colorful culture and history. The opportunities are endless, there is a lot to do for everyone on Zanzibar. We selected for you the best Zanzibar excursions.
blocks.html: Zanzibar, the tropical island, is famous for its lovely white beaches and coral reefs. Yet besides relaxed beach life and water sports, it also has a colourful history and culture. There is no end to the possibilities, and everyone will find plenty to do on Zanzibar. Below is our selection of the best excursions on Zanzibar.

blocks.orig:
Spice tour
Visit a spice farm and learn how spices, herbs and fruits grow and used as medicine.
blocks.html:
Spice tour
Head to a spice farm and find out how spices, herbs and fruit are grown and used as medicine.

blocks.orig:
Kite surfing
Thanks to its steady sideshore winds, Zanzibar is an ideal spot for wind- or kitesurfing, especially the beaches at Paje, Kiwengwa and Nungwi.
blocks.html:
Kitesurfing
With its constant sideshore winds, Zanzibar is perfect for windsurfing or kitesurfing, above all on the beaches of Paje, Kiwengwa and Nungwi.

blocks.orig:
Mountainbike tour
If you like some exercise and adventure go on a biking tour to explore the island. It offers you a nice insight in the daily way of life and beautiful nature.
blocks.html:
Mountain bike tour
Fancy a bit of exercise and adventure? Explore the island on a bike tour. You get a good look at everyday life and at the lovely natural surroundings.

blocks.orig:
Walking tour in Stonetown
The old Stone Town is the historical centre of Zanzibar and an amazing mix of Food lovers and culture enthusiasts can visit interesting cultural places like Sultan’s Palace, the House of Wonders, the Slave Market and Darajani or Forodhani food markets. You can ever dinner at Freddie Mercury’s former house, who was born in Zanzibar.
blocks.html:
Stone Town walking tour
Zanzibar's historical heart is the old Stone Town, a truly amazing mix. Food lovers and culture fans alike can explore fascinating cultural spots such as the Sultan’s Palace, the House of Wonders, the Slave Market and the Darajani or Forodhani food markets. You can even have dinner in the former home of Freddie Mercury, who was born on Zanzibar.

blocks.orig:
Prison Island
Visit the deserted island that was once used as a place where slaves were detained. Nowadays Prison Island is a place to relax at the lovely white beach. It is ideal for snorkeling, swimming or sunbathing. You can also see the old prison ruins and about hundred giant land tortoise.
blocks.html:
Prison Island
Pay a visit to this uninhabited island, where slaves were once held. Today, Prison Island is a spot for relaxing on its pretty white beach, perfect for snorkelling, swimming or sunbathing. You can also see the ruins of the old prison and around a hundred giant land tortoises.

blocks.orig:
Safari Blue
Enjoy the natural beauty of Zanzibar on a traditional wooden sailboat (dhow). Visit 3 beautiful island where you can swim, snorkel and enjoy an delicious barbecue. Another popular snorkeling trip is to Mnemba Atoll, one of the most beautiful snorkel spots in Zanzibar.
blocks.html:
Safari Blue
Take in the natural beauty of Zanzibar aboard a traditional wooden sailing boat (dhow). You stop at 3 lovely islands to swim, snorkel and tuck into a tasty barbecue. Mnemba Atoll, one of the finest snorkelling spots on Zanzibar, is another popular snorkelling trip.

blocks.orig:
Jozani Forest
Go on a walk through the last indigenous forest and mangroves on Zanzibar. The huge palms in this forest are impressive and you will see lots of monkeys like the rare Red Colobus Monkeys.
blocks.html:
Jozani Forest
Walk through the last native forest and mangroves of Zanzibar. The enormous palms here are a striking sight, and you will see many monkeys, including the rare red colobus monkey.

blocks.orig:
Restaurant The Rock
This restaurant is built on a rock in the ocean. An awesome place to eat and enjoy the views.
blocks.html:
The Rock restaurant
Set on a rock in the sea, this restaurant is a great spot to have a meal and take in the view.

blocks.orig:
Chumbe Island
This uninhabited small coral island is a true snorkeling paradise. It is the first private marine park in the world and has only 7 beautiful eco-friendly bungalows, surround by pristine nature.
blocks.html:
Chumbe Island
A small, uninhabited coral island that is a real paradise for snorkellers. It was the first private marine park in the world and has just 7 lovely eco-friendly bungalows, set in untouched nature.

blocks.orig: The most popular time to visit Zanzibar is during the dry season, from June to October and from December to February. However, Zanzibar Island is a great beach destination all-year round. Even during the wet season (mid-March, April, May, November) it is beautiful, since the rain showers don’t last much longer than 30 minutes and the temperatures still remain around 28 C. February is the hottest month in Zanzibar (average 28 C), while July (average 24 C) is the coldest. Given its tropical climate, it’s always a good time to visit Zanzibar.
blocks.html: The dry season, from June to October and from December to February, is the busiest time to visit Zanzibar. That said, the island makes a great beach destination throughout the year. The wet season (mid-March, April, May, November) is lovely too, as showers rarely last more than 30 minutes and temperatures stay at around 28 C. The hottest month on Zanzibar is February (average 28 C) and the coolest is July (average 24 C). Thanks to the tropical climate, any time is a good time to go.

blocks.orig: Zanzibar offers a wealth of lodges, hotels and resorts. It has everything ranging from basic accommodation to ultra-luxury. Your Tanzania Trip knows most of the accommodation Zanzibar so you can always contact us for advice. We prefer the personal atmosphere of the small bed & breakfast lodges on the island. The staff is so friendly and will do everything you make sure you have a great time. Another benefit of bed & breakfasts is that you can explore other restaurants and bars during the day and evening. There are so many great places to eat and have a drink, with beautiful views over the ocean and a great ambiance.
blocks.html: On Zanzibar you can choose from a huge range of lodges, hotels and resorts, from simple places to stay right up to ultra-luxury. As Your Tanzania Trip knows most of the accommodation on Zanzibar, you are always welcome to ask us for advice. Our own preference is the personal feel of the island's small bed & breakfast lodges. The staff are very friendly and go out of their way to make sure you enjoy your stay. A further advantage of bed & breakfasts is that you are free to try other restaurants and bars during the day and in the evening. There are lots of great places to eat and drink, with lovely ocean views and a great atmosphere.

blocks.orig: “Zanzibar is a fantastic, beautiful island. I stayed in the village Jambiani and the Zanzibari (local people) are so friendly and welcoming. They are always up for a chat. The beaches, spice farms, forests and little villages are so beautiful. The only drawback i can think of is the lack of museums, but it can also be I did not went to the right places. There are so many nice restaurants and bars on the island where you can eat delicious local or western meals and dance.”
blocks.html: “Zanzibar is a wonderful, beautiful island. I stayed in Jambiani village, and the Zanzibari (the local people) are incredibly friendly and welcoming, always happy to have a chat. The beaches, spice farms, forests and small villages are all lovely. The one downside I can think of is that there are not many museums, though maybe I just did not visit the right places. The island has lots of nice restaurants and bars where you can enjoy tasty local or western food and go dancing.”

blocks.orig: “Zanzibar is a great beach destination you don’t want to miss when you visit Tanzania. It is a paradise and the perfect place to end your safari. We stayed at the eastcoast of the island where you can find amazing beaches. The beaches are pretty quiet with no annoying beach boys. We have eaten delicious sea food for a fair price at several restaurants.”
blocks.html: “If you visit Tanzania, Zanzibar is a great beach destination you shouldn't skip. It is a paradise and an ideal way to round off your safari. We stayed on the east coast, where the beaches are amazing. They are fairly quiet and there are no annoying beach boys. At several restaurants we enjoyed tasty seafood at a fair price.”
